If you can point me to a runbook, CI config, or deployment docs, I'll read them and save the details so I can answer properly next time. Or if you'd rather just tell me, I'll note it down.

If a health check fails on a node, the system retries it twice with a short pause between attempts. If it passes on the second try, the deploy continues to the next node.

If it fails both retries, the deploy halts immediately — that node stays running the old version, and no further nodes get updated. The on-call gets paged with the node ID, the failing endpoint, and the last few lines of logs. The deploy job also leaves the cluster in a "paused" state so nobody accidentally resumes it without looking at the problem first.
